messages:
josh (support): FYI customer 'BlueQuarry' reporting p99 jump for Lyra3 after yesterday's model flip. p95 ~450ms -> 1.9s, p99 ~1.8s -> 8.2s. Only happens on very long inputs (>32k tokens). sample req: req_0a7f3c.

amanda (eng-runtime): thx. Any errors in logs or 5xx?

josh (support): No 5xx. Calls succeed but streaming stalls for minutes sometimes, then finishes. No 401/429. They provided a minimal curl to repro.

raj (eng-ml): can you paste the curl and example payload? curious if tokenizer change triggers fallback path.

josh (support): pasted below:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"lyra3-v1.1","input":"<very long doc ~38k tokens>","stream":true}'
```

josh (support): They said it was fine on lyra2 and lyra3-v1.0, regressed after v1.1 and our tokenizer bump (subword-norm v2).

amanda (eng-runtime): I ran quick traces on their request id in prod logs. I see continuous KV cache misses and a kernel path that flips to slow token normalization at chunk boundaries. attaching condensed trace: 

```
TRACE req_0a7f3c: tokenize -> norm_subword_v2 -> chunk_split -> kv_cache_miss (x22) -> schedule small batches -> stall 7s -> resume
```

maria (sre): looks like kv key churn — segmenter outputs inconsistent segment ids for identical prefixes because of normalization change. cache hit rate drops to ~12% for >32k. That explains token regen and scheduling thrash (small batches).

raj (eng-ml): Interesting. Tokenizer v2 introduced iterative normalization for CJK/emoji sequences; it's O(n^2) at pathological boundaries when run per-segment. On short contexts it's fine; at long contexts the segmenter causes the server to re-tokenize overlapping windows, producing different KV keys and forcing recompute.

amanda (eng-runtime): Repro plan: 1) reproduce on canary with their input 2) instrument kv key generation to log segment hash 3) toggle tokenizer flag `norm_v2=false` at runtime to see if hit rate recovers.

sre-bot: Canary deployment lyra3-v1.1-canary started on us-west-2. ID: canary-2026-03-17-02

josh (support): Customer ok with canary test.

maria (sre): Quick mitigation options while we fix tokenizer: 
- rollback model routing to lyra3-v1.0 for that customer (fast)
- force `norm_v2=false` on lyra3-v1.1 for long-context requests (>16k) (runtime flag)
- enable prefix-anchored KV hashing (reduce churn)
- instruct customer to truncate to last 16k tokens (temporary customer-side mitigation)

raj (eng-ml): For long-term: patch tokenizer to produce stable segment boundaries (idempotent normalization across windows). Also add regression test with 100k-char CJK+emoji mix.

amanda (eng-runtime): I toggled norm_v2=false on canary. Re-running their payload — p99 dropped from 8.2s to 1.1s, kv hit rate jumped to 78%. Looks like root cause confirmed.

josh (support): I told customer we can: pivot their traffic to lyra3-v1.0 immediately or keep on v1.1 with the runtime toggle until a tokenizer patch ships. They prefer staying on v1.1 if perf restored.

maria (sre): I'll open a quick incident ticket and schedule rollback window as contingency. Ticket: INC-2026-0456.

raj (eng-ml): I'll start a fix branch for tokenizer stable-boundaries and add unit + fuzz tests. ETA for patch: 2 business days, can land hotfix in 24-36h if QA passes.

amanda (eng-runtime): Ops actions: 
- apply `norm_v2=false` on lyra3-v1.1 in prod rollout config for requests >16k tokens (done on canary, awaiting approval)
- add KV stable-hash flag to runtime as toggle (low risk)
- add alert for kv hit rate <25% for a model route

josh (support): Customer updated: happy with runtime toggle. Thanks team. I'll keep thread updated and attach their request sample + billing id for correlation.

ingest-bot: Logged customer repro payload to secure bucket s3://redwood-support/bluequarry/repro/req_0a7f3c.json

maria (sre): Closing immediate high-severity escalation once routing change confirmed. Leaving follow-ups for eng-ml patch + e2e tests.

josh (support): Marking this resolved for now. Will reopen if customer sees further regressions. :white_check_mark:
